ENT CLINICAL NOTE

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure: Sudden‐onset central chest pressure while gardening; possible exertional trigger.
- Symptom timeline and progression: Began “a couple of hours” prior to call; pressure rated 7/10 and persistent at time of consult.
- ENT symptoms: 
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: Denied.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: Not reported.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia: Denied difficulty swallowing or drinking water.  
  • Drooling: Not reported.  
  • Nasal/ocular symptoms: Not reported.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing: Denied.  
  • Dyspnea: Present; unchanged during call; worsens on exertion (stairs, hills).  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: Denied.  
  • Ear/neck symptoms: Denied.  
- Associated non-ENT symptoms: Left shoulder/arm pain, light-headedness, nausea without vomiting, bilateral calf pain and leg swelling with exertion (historical).
- Relevant past episodes and treatments: None reported.
- Past medical history: Hypertension and hypercholesterolemia; not on medication.
- Allergies: “None mentioned” (not documented).
- Current medications: None.
- Social context: Lives with wife; wife present at home.

Objective:
- Observable swelling: Not reported.
- Airway/breathing: Patient speaking in full sentences; reports shortness of breath; no stridor noted.
- Mental status: Alert; complains of light-headedness.
- Vitals/exam findings: Not recorded.
- Others present: Wife at home (not on call).

Assessment:
- Central chest pressure with dyspnea in patient with hypertension/hypercholesterolemia; cardiac etiology most likely (non-ENT).  
- No evidence of acute upper-airway obstruction or ENT emergency at this time.

Plan:
- Immediate action: Physician initiated emergency ambulance dispatch for hospital evaluation.
- Patient advised:  
  • Remain calm, stay on phone until EMS arrival.  
  • Inform wife, prepare to accompany to hospital.  
  • Avoid taking any medications prior to EMS arrival.  
  • Sip water as needed.  
- Escalation/red flags reviewed: Worsening chest pain, breathing difficulty, new throat swelling, voice change, or syncope—seek immediate help (ambulance already en route).
- Follow-up: Hospital assessment by consultant on arrival; virtual follow-up appointment to be scheduled post-hospitalization.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing expected elements:  
  – Detailed allergy list.  
  – Current/past ENT-specific conditions, prior anaphylaxis history.  
  – Medication list confirmation (including OTC).  
  – Vital signs, focused airway examination.  
● Internal conflicts: Date of birth 07-Jun-1974 would make patient 48 (2022) vs patient’s stated age 53/54 – conflict noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor overlaps but clinically adequate.
